messages:
maya (Support): escalating from support — customer reported Dedicated capacity console shows 0 nodes / 0 GPUs for their pool after a recent cluster change. they drained and uncordoned nodes as part of a kubelet rollout. customer says pods are running on nodes but the dashboard node list is empty and GPU inventory is missing. quote from customer: 'we rolled kubelet 1.22.x -> 1.22.y, drained nodes one-by-one, uncordoned. console now shows 0 GPUs and blank node list even though `kubectl get nodes` shows 8 nodes with nvidia.com/gpu allocatable.'

ben (SRE): thanks — can you paste cluster id and approximate timestamps? also check if any labels/taints were changed on the pool. first quick checks: `kubectl get nodes -o wide` and `kubectl get nodes -o json | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, allocatable: .status.allocatable}'` — confirm GPU allocatable on k8s level. check dedicated controller & inventory exporter logs: `kubectl -n redwood logs deployment/dedicated-controller` and `kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=inventory-exporter`.

maya (Support): cluster: rdw-dedicated-nyc-prod pool id: pool-72f. incident started ~1718049000 (customer local). customer provided `kubectl get nodes` snippet:
```
NAME                          STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION    ALLOCATABLE
gke-pool-72f-0                Ready    <none>   12h   v1.22.14   cpu: 32, memory: 126Gi, nvidia.com/gpu: 8
gke-pool-72f-1                Ready    <none>   12h   v1.22.14   cpu: 32, memory: 126Gi, nvidia.com/gpu: 8
... (total 8 nodes)
```
but console UI (Dedicated -> Pools -> pool-72f -> Nodes) shows empty list and metrics panels show "No data" for GPU utilization.

carla (Platform): possible causes: inventory ingestion backlog, sequence id mismatch after node rollout, or the exporter failed to emit GPU keys (label rename?). check inventory API directly: `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://internal-api.redwood/pools/pool-72f/inventory | jq .` — see if API returns nodes. also check configmap for inventory-exporter to see if scrape/label mapping changed during rollout.

observability-bot: inventory.events.backlog: 13420
inventory.last_processed_ts: 1718047400
ingestion-lag: 10m 45s

ben (SRE): that backlog is suspicious — if exporter crashed while nodes were drained, events could have been dropped and the controller may have rejected out-of-order sequence numbers. please get dedicated-controller logs around `skipping event: seq mismatch` or `event older than lastProcessed`.

maya (Support): i pulled logs from staging repro. reproduced by draining + uncordon with a daemonset update. excerpt from dedicated-controller log:
```
I0305 14:05:11.123 controller.go:412] processing inventory event seq=78512 pool=pool-72f
W0305 14:05:11.124 controller.go:421] skipping event: sequence mismatch (expected 78513, got 78512)
E0305 14:05:11.125 controller.go:430] failed to apply inventory batch: dropped 8 events due to seq gap
```
so controller dropped events instead of triggering a full resync.

carla (Platform): we should push a two-part mitigation: 1) trigger a manual full resync for the affected pool (internal endpoint): `POST /internal/pools/pool-72f/refresh-inventory` — this will repopulate node/gpu inventory from cluster snapshot; 2) patch controller to tolerate small seq gaps by enqueuing resync on gap detection. i'll draft a canary patch for staging and then prod.

ben (SRE): agreed. i'll run the POST on staging now and roll the patch to canary. steps i'll take:
- run `kubectl -n redwood exec -it deployment/dedicated-controller -- /bin/controllerctl resync --pool pool-72f`
- monitor inventory backfill: `kubectl -n redwood logs -f deployment/inventory-exporter` and check metrics `inventory.events.processed_total`.

maya (Support): i'll update the customer with the workaround (manual refresh) and ETA for the patch. they want a root cause note and a ticket link. adding support ticket ID #SUP-2387 to the thread.

deploy-bot: deploy event: dedicated-controller v1.9.2 -> v1.9.3 canary started by ben at 1718051600 :rocket:

ben (SRE): canary looks good on staging; inventory API returned nodes and console panels repopulated after resync. still validating edgecases for drifted sequence numbers. will schedule a prod canary tomorrow 09:00 PT and follow rollback playbook if we see >1% failure.

maya (Support): thanks team — updating customer with manual-refresh instructions + next steps. :thumbsup:
